members.name: Agnieszka

members.thread: A bookkeeping and HR service from the writing desk upstairs.

members.name: Tomasz
members.thread: An IoT consultant at the octagonal table in the sunroom.

character.lede: An eco-modern house stands on a raised plinth, a sage board tower between a glass living wing and the entry. Rust-shingle roofs, a split-level garage and tropical foundation beds surround it, with a hammock on the deck.

spots.line: An L-shaped sectional, an octagonal table and rattan chairs fill the sunroom.
A writing desk and a ladderback chair stand against the wall.
A workbench, a bicycle and tool hooks fill the garage.

facts.style: Two-storey eco-modern on a raised plinth: a projecting sage board tower between a one-storey glass living wing and a recessed double-door entry up broad dark timber steps, a cascade of rust-shingle roofs edged in thick chocolate fascia with glazed gable ends, a split-level garage with a loft dormer, tropical foundation beds and palms on a seaside lot

character.truths: The Core sits on a shelf in the Sunroom Lounge, in sight of the door. There is no television. The kitchen has an island. A hammock and a fire bowl on the deck; the garage is split-level.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

nextcloud: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Nextcloud as a recommended app.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
open-webui: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Open WebUI as a featured app.
[cloud-link] It can also connect to cloud models with an API key. Leave that off.
[note] Wired to the Core's local model by the Hub (hub_integration inference). Say "a model on the Core"; never claim it matches a hosted model and never give a speed figure.
Can connect to cloud models with an API key (field in the install form): leave out of any scene.
Hub wires it to the local model.
donetick: [cloud-link] Notifications use Telegram or Pushover. Both are outside services.
NFC-tag completion needs a phone that reads NFC on the home network
homehub: No passwords: a "Select your user" box offers every name including Administrator (anyone on the network can pick one)
Extras bundled: recipes, expiry tracker, link shortener, PDF compressor, QR generator
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
monetr: marketplace: Replaces lists Mint, which Intuit retired in 2024.
marketplace: Licence is the Functional Source License (not open source).
twenty: marketplace: QA capture shows real company names and logos.
activepieces: [note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
Listing says "Secure by Design ... network-gapped": over-claim, do not repeat.
Overlaps n8n: name one automation tool per household.
AI pieces call outside model providers if a key is added; leave that out of any scene.
akaunting: [claims] Bookkeeping tool. No accounting, tax or legal advice.
marketplace: Source-available (Business Source License). Seafile and others carry umbrel strings: the admin email default is a placeholder address on umbrel.local.
libreoffice: [note] The listing is generic. Name the suite, not specific features.
[note] ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors does the same job: one suite per household.
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
frigate: [hardware] Needs IP cameras that stream over RTSP. Cameras are not part of the Core.
[public-access] Watching cameras from away from home is remote access, which the sheet leaves unfinished.
[claims] No detection-speed or accuracy numbers. Do not say it prevents anything.
QA screenshot shows "No frames have been received, check error logs": reject. The store listing image shows a real backyard photo that is not a Hub capture.
Watching away from home is remote access: not claimed.
stirling-pdf: QA screenshot is a sign-in wall that prints default credentials
already in the persona pool: share cap risk
influxdb2: QA screenshot is the welcome page.
Needs something writing to it (Home Assistant or sensors).
glasshome: Listing and notes say entity data never leaves the network: do not repeat the absolute.
Optional community widgets come from an outside hub.
hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core
Heavy for a client tool: three containers
cryptpad: Listing says "end-to-end encrypted": banned wording (f-security-guarantee), do not repeat
Collaboration with people outside the home needs outside reach
lubelogger: Do not claim savings or economy figures
No sign-in until the user sets one (unverified)
photoview: [cloud-link] Map view uses a Mapbox token you can add. Leave it off for a fully local gallery.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Public sharing links need inbound reach: keep out of stories
Face recognition is a feature, not a claim to amplify
blinko: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
AI search and chat need a model provider added in the app (OpenAI, Ollama, LiteLLM...): not wired by the Hub.
No QA run; gallery frame is upstream marketing with a "#Password" tagged note and a gmail file name: reject.
Companion desktop and mobile clients are separate downloads.
cryptgeon: Notes live only in RAM: a restart of the app wipes every unread note
Do not repeat the listing's encryption wording (sec-absolute); say a note opens once and is gone
Overlaps Enclosed and PrivateBin: one burn-after-reading tool per household
searxng: [cloud-link] It queries outside search engines for you. Say "private search", not "offline search".
cloud-link: the engines still see the query from the Core
listing says users are not tracked: do not repeat
